previous_description: Defines password complexity, rotation, and lockout requirements for credential-based authentication. Implements NIST SP 800-53 IA-5(1) controls including minimum length, character class requirements, history enforcement, and brute-force lockout thresholds.
definition: A credential rule set that fixes the length bounds, required character classes, reuse history, expiry interval and failed-attempt lockout for memorized secrets (passwords or passphrases) accepted by an authenticator. It covers only the rules a password must satisfy and how repeated failures are handled, not how the principal is authenticated overall.

distinguish_from.when: the symbol configures the identity provider, MFA, session timeout or verification level, of which password rules are at most one referenced part.
a regex, length or range check validates an ordinary data field rather than the composition of a login credential.
the code implements a general brute-force or credential-stuffing mitigation (IP throttling, CAPTCHA, breached-password screening) not expressed as password composition or account lockout parameters.

standard_reference: NIST SP 800-53 IA-5(1) Password-Based Authentication (with AC-7 Unsuccessful Logon Attempts for lockout)
code_evidence: Framework password option blocks such as Django AUTH_PASSWORD_VALIDATORS (MinimumLengthValidator), ASP.NET Identity PasswordOptions/LockoutOptions, or Spring Security password constraint beans.

Identity-provider or infrastructure declarations such as a Keycloak realm passwordPolicy string ('length(12) and upperCase(1) and passwordHistory(5)'), an AWS Cognito PasswordPolicy block, or a Terraform aws_iam_account_password_policy resource.

A password-change or registration routine that tests character-class regexes, compares the new hash against stored previous hashes, and returns messages like 'Password must contain a special character', or a failed-login counter that sets a locked-until timestamp.

attribute_descriptions.name: minLength
attribute_descriptions.description: Minimum number of characters a password must contain; set whenever a lower length bound is enforced (NIST SP 800-63B suggests at least 8, commonly 12+).

attribute_descriptions.name: maxLength
attribute_descriptions.description: Maximum number of characters accepted for a password; set only when the system caps length, and leave unset if no cap exists.

attribute_descriptions.name: requireUppercase
attribute_descriptions.description: True when a password must contain at least one uppercase letter (A-Z); omit or set false when no such rule is enforced.

attribute_descriptions.name: requireLowercase
attribute_descriptions.description: True when a password must contain at least one lowercase letter (a-z); omit or set false when no such rule is enforced.

attribute_descriptions.name: requireNumbers
attribute_descriptions.description: True when a password must contain at least one decimal digit (0-9); omit or set false when no such rule is enforced.

attribute_descriptions.name: requireSpecialChars
attribute_descriptions.description: True when a password must contain at least one non-alphanumeric symbol; omit or set false when no such rule is enforced.

attribute_descriptions.name: preventReuse
attribute_descriptions.description: Number of previous passwords per account that a new password may not match; 0 or unset means no history check.

attribute_descriptions.name: expiryDays
attribute_descriptions.description: Number of days after which a password must be changed; use 0 when passwords never expire by age.

attribute_descriptions.name: lockoutAttempts
attribute_descriptions.description: Number of consecutive failed authentication attempts that triggers account lockout; leave unset when no lockout is enforced.

attribute_descriptions.name: lockoutDuration
attribute_descriptions.description: Length of time, in minutes, that an account stays locked after reaching lockoutAttempts; use 0 when unlock requires administrator action.

notes: expiryDays is required, yet NIST SP 800-63B discourages forced periodic rotation; make it optional with 0 meaning no expiry. lockoutDuration has no declared unit. Lockout belongs to AC-7, not IA-5(1). Consider adding breached-password screening. The 'mandates' and 'requires' relationships to countermeasure duplicate each other.
